items.title: Four Candidates, Including Three Newcomers, Vie for Mississauga's PDSB Trustee Seat in Wards 2 and 8
items.summary: According to mississauga.com, four candidates are running to represent Mississauga's Wards 2 and 8 on the Peel District School Board ahead of the October 26 municipal election. The paper identifies the candidates as Tamer Elkateb, Samantha Fung, Brad MacDonald and Michael Michalias. Mississauga.com's parent company, Metroland Media, sent each candidate a set of basic background questions as part of its election coverage, the paper says. The single trustee seat covers both Ward 2 and Ward 8, meaning whoever wins will represent students and families across both areas on the school board. Voters in those two wards will choose among the four candidates when they cast their ballots on Election Day, according to the paper.

items.title: City Hall Lights Up Orange as Mississauga Lines Up Library Talks, Museum Tours and a Flag Raising for Truth and Reconciliation Day
items.summary: According to mississauga.com, Mississauga is hosting several gatherings and sessions ahead of the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation on September 30, also known as Orange Shirt Day. City Hall will be lit in orange to mark the occasion, the paper reports. At the Hazel McCallion Central Library on Burnhamthorpe Road West, attendees can learn about the importance of Truth and Reconciliation through stories and shared reflection, with in-person enrolment available on a first-come, first-served basis and orange shirts encouraged. The Bradley Museum will offer tours every 30 minutes covering the history of Indigenous peoples in present-day Mississauga and the museum's ongoing work on the 94 Calls to Action, with free admission and walk-ins welcome, though reservations are recommended. At Celebration Square and the Civic Centre, the city will raise the flag of the Mississaugas of the Credit First Nation to mark the day, followed that evening by an orange illumination of the Clock Tower. Digital screens at Celebration Square will also display the 94 Calls to Action, according to the paper.

items.title: MiWay Blames Visa Rule Changes and Manufacturing Job Losses for a Year-Over-Year Ridership Drop
items.summary: According to mississauga.com, MiWay has recorded a year-over-year decline in ridership, based on a new quarterly report presented to the city's transit advisory committee. City staff pointed to several factors behind the drop, including federal changes to international student visa rules, job losses in the manufacturing and warehousing sectors, higher youth unemployment, and net population losses across the province that have lowered daily travel demand. The paper reports that the ridership decline is also affecting the city's finances, based on a separate June 2026 financial report prepared for the same committee. Mississauga.com notes the figures were presented as part of the committee's regular review of transit performance and budget impacts. Staff did not attribute the decline to any single cause, instead describing it as the result of several factors converging at once, according to the paper.

items.title: Damerla's $31K in Taxpayer-Funded Social Media Spending Fuels Mississauga Transparency Debate
items.summary: According to The Pointer, Mississauga mayoral candidate and city councillor Dipika Damerla has spent more than $31,000 in taxpayer money on social media over the current four-year council term, while other councillors reported thousands of dollars in similar expenses. The outlet reports that public records it reviewed identify the nature of the spending without naming the vendors involved. Damerla told The Pointer she views the spending as a key way to support democratic engagement with residents. The Pointer says councillors argue social media has become essential for reaching constituents, particularly younger residents, as traditional communication methods like printed newsletters become less effective. Trevor Isaac, vice chair of the ratepayer group MIRANET, told The Pointer that residents need more information about how councillors are using social media and how that public money is being spent. The Pointer frames the spending as part of a broader transparency debate at city hall heading into the October 26 municipal election.

items.title: Peel Police Shut Down Westbound Dundas at Tomken After a Pedestrian Is Critically Hurt
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police, a pedestrian was struck by a vehicle in the area of Dundas Street and Tomken Road in Mississauga and taken to hospital with life-threatening injuries. Police say the collision prompted them to close all westbound lanes on Dundas Street west of Tomken Road while they investigate. No additional details about the victim have been released, according to police. Officers are urging drivers to avoid the area while the road remains closed. Peel police are asking anyone with information about the crash to contact them directly, and tips can also be submitted anonymously through Crime Stoppers, which police say can pay a reward of up to $2,000 for information leading to an arrest.
